transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Well… mostly it’s my eating, I guess. It’s gotten all turned around lately. Some days I’ll just forget lunch completely, and then other days I’m standing at the counter eating crackers or little sweets, just picking at them, even though nothing really tastes right.

I was telling myself maybe it’s just age or the weather changing—I used to make proper lunches, you know, soup and a sandwich—but now it’s like I can’t keep track of it the same way. That’s what made me think I should come in.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yes… I suppose I have. Most mornings I wake up and there’s this heavy, low feeling, like the day has already gone gray before I’ve even put my slippers on. I’ll sit on the edge of the bed longer than I mean to.

It’s funny, I used to like opening the curtains right away—my neighbor has those little red flowers out front, geraniums I think—but lately I just look at the light and it doesn’t feel like much of anything. So… yes, down, I guess that’s the word.
Have you been feeling more tired than usual or noticed a loss of energy, even if you haven’t done much physically?

I don’t know if I’d call it tired exactly. I mean, I do sit down a lot, but I’ve always been one to have my little chair by the window. My mother had a chair like that too, with a crocheted blanket over the back—funny the things you remember.

Energy… I’m not sure. Some days I don’t get much done, but I couldn’t say if that’s being tired or just not getting around to it. I haven’t really noticed it in a clear way.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or have others commented that you seem slowed down or restless?

Yes… I think so. I don’t know if anyone’s said it exactly, but I feel slow in myself. Like crossing the room takes me longer than it should, or I’ll be trying to button my sweater and my fingers just… don’t get on with it.

Though then other times I catch myself pacing around the house with papers in my hand, the same papers, not really doing anything with them. I used to sort mail right at the little table by the door—my husband always put receipts in the wrong place, drove me mad—but now I’ll just carry things around. So yes, slowed down, and sometimes a bit restless too, I suppose.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight recently?

Yes, my eating’s been… all turned around, I suppose. That’s part of why I came in, really.

Some days I’ll get to late afternoon and realize I never had lunch at all, which is silly because I’ve got soup in the cupboard and those little tins of peaches I used to like. And then other days I’m standing at the counter eating crackers, or something sweet, just one after another, though it doesn’t even taste right. I don’t know about my weight exactly—I don’t keep track like I should—but the appetite part, yes, it’s been strange.
Have you been feeling like you’re not worth much lately, or like you’ve let people down even if you don’t know how?

I don’t know… “not worth much” sounds so strong, doesn’t it? I mean, I have days where I look around and think I should have done more, but then there’s always something that needs doing, isn’t there?

Let people down… I’m not sure. My daughter says I’m too hard on myself, but she says that about the way I fold towels too, so I don’t know. We used to keep the linen cupboard very neat—my mother had a whole way of doing pillowcases. I suppose I sometimes feel bad when things aren’t kept up, but I wouldn’t say I know for sure that I’ve let anyone down.
Have you found that things you used to enjoy, like your chair by the window or sorting the mail, don’t give you the same pleasure they used to?

Yes… I suppose that’s true. It’s not so much the chair, though I do sit there and not really notice the light the way I used to.

I used to look forward to my watercolor class, and the quilting circle, and book club too—though book club sometimes spent more time talking about whose grandson was moving where than the book itself. I’d get my little bag ready by the door, with the folder or the fabric pieces, and now it just… sits there. I see it when I pass by, and I think, “I should go,” but I can’t seem to care enough to pick it up and leave. It feels like too much, or like it won’t matter if I go or not.
Would you say that your mood has been down most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Most mornings, yes… I wake up and it’s like there’s this heaviness already there, before I’ve even put my feet on the floor. Like the day’s lost its color somehow.

I used to notice the little patch of sun on the dresser—well, when the curtains were open right—but lately I just lie there thinking, “Oh, it’s morning again.” So yes, I suppose it is down a lot of the day, most days.
Would you say that you’ve lost interest in most things, like even the ones you used to really enjoy, such as your watercolor class or seeing friends from the quilting circle?

Yes… I think so. I used to look forward to those things, especially watercolor class. I’d have my little bag ready by the door with my brushes, or the fabric pieces for quilting, and sometimes the book for book club—though half the time I’d forget which chapter we were meant to read.

Now the bag just sits there. I see it, and I think I ought to go, people will be expecting me maybe, but I just… can’t make myself care enough to pick it up and leave. It feels strange, because I did enjoy it before. The quilting ladies are nice, even if they do talk over each other terribly. But lately I just let the time pass.
How long have you been feeling this way — this heaviness in the morning and losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Oh… it’s been a while now. I keep thinking it started just after last winter, but then I remember the garden catalogs were already coming in, and I didn’t even care to look at the roses.

I’d say… about a year and two months. That low, colorless feeling has sort of been hanging around that long. It’s odd how time passes when you’re not really marking it by things anymore.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately, like waking up too early or not being able to fall asleep?

I’m not really sure how to answer that exactly. Some nights I look at the clock and then I forget what time it said, and other nights I just remember the room being dark for a long time.

I used to keep a little notepad by the bed for grocery things—milk, stamps, cat food, though I don’t have a cat anymore, that was years ago—but I haven’t been writing anything down lately. So… I don’t know if I’m waking too early or just noticing it more. Sleep hasn’t felt very clear to me, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed any significant weight loss or gain recently, even if your eating habits have changed?

I don’t know about the number exactly… I haven’t been very good about the scale. It’s in the bathroom, but there’s a stack of old towels in front of it, and I keep meaning to move them.

But my eating has gotten all turned around. Some days I forget lunch completely, and then other days I’m just standing at the counter eating crackers or sweets, like those little vanilla cookies, even though they don’t really taste right. I don’t even sit down with a proper plate half the time. It’s part of why I thought maybe I should come in, because that isn’t like how I used to be.
